result.story:
Anna und Ben sind am Bahnhof. Sie wollen zusammen fahren. Anna hat zwei Fahrkarten in der Hand.

„Wohin fahren wir?“, fragt Ben.

Anna sieht auf ihre Fahrkarte. „Mein Ziel ist Berlin.“

Ben sieht auf seine Fahrkarte. „Mein Ziel ist Bonn.“

Die Ziele sind verschieden. Anna und Ben sehen sich an.

„Wir fahren nicht zum gleichen Ziel“, sagt Anna.

Ben sieht auf die Anzeige. „Der Zug nach Berlin kommt gleich. Und der Zug nach Bonn kommt auch bald.“

Anna hält ihre Fahrkarte fest. Ben sieht auf die beiden Züge. „Welchen Zug nehmen wir?“

glossary.meaning: railway station; the place where the friends wait for their trains.
ticket for a journey by train.
destination; the place someone is travelling to.
train.
to be; “sind” is used with “Anna und Ben,” and “ist” with “Mein Ziel.”
to want to; here, to plan or intend to travel together.
together, as a group or pair.
to travel or go, here by train.
to have or hold; Anna has the tickets with her.
in someone’s hand; being held.
where to; asks about a destination or direction.
to ask a question.
to look or see; “sieht auf” means looks at.
to look at something; here, to check a ticket or the display.
my; shows that something belongs to or is associated with the speaker.
his; here, it shows that the ticket belongs to Ben.
different from one another; the two destinations do not match.
to look at one another.
not; makes a statement negative.
the same; in “zum gleichen Ziel,” it means the same destination.
to say or tell someone something.
to; used before a place to show where a train is going.
to come or arrive; here, for a train to reach the station.
soon; the train is expected shortly.
also or too; adds that the train to Bonn is coming as well.
soon, but not necessarily immediately.
to hold; “hält … fest” means keeps a firm hold on something.
to hold on tightly.
both; the two trains together.
which; used to ask someone to choose from a set of options.
to take or choose; here, to choose a train to travel on.
at the railway station; “am” is a short form of “an dem.”
